knitr::opts_chunk$set(message = FALSE, warning=FALSE)
# plotly.js from the CDN, so the site's pages don't each copy it

A [Choropleth Map](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Choropleth_map) is a map composed of colored polygons. It is used to represent spatial variations of a quantity. This page documents how to build **outline** choropleth maps, but you can also build [choropleth **tile maps** using `add_choroplethmap()`](mapbox-county-choropleth.html).

### Base Map Configuration

plotly.core figures have a `layout.geo` object (built with `go_geo()` and set with `update_layout(geo = ...)` or `update_geos()`) which can be used to control the appearance of the base map onto which data is plotted.

### Introduction: main parameters for choropleth outline maps

Making choropleth maps requires two main types of input:

1. Geometry information:
   1. This can either be a supplied GeoJSON file where each feature has either an `id` field or some identifying value in `properties`; or
   2. one of the built-in geometries within plotly.js: US states and world countries (see below)
2. A list of values indexed by feature identifier.

The GeoJSON data is passed to the `geojson` argument, and the data is passed into the `z` argument of choropleth traces.

**Note** the `geojson` attribute can also be the URL to a GeoJSON file, which can speed up map rendering in certain cases.

### GeoJSON with `feature.id`

Here we load a GeoJSON file containing the geometry information for US counties, where `feature.id` is a [FIPS code](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FIPS_county_code).

```{r}
library(plotly.core)
library(jsonlite)

data <- fromJSON(
  "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/plotly/datasets/master/geojson-counties-fips.json",
  simplifyVector = FALSE
)
data$features[[1]]
```

#### Data indexed by `id`

Here we load unemployment data by county, also indexed by [FIPS code](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FIPS_county_code).

```{r}
df <- read.csv(
  "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/plotly/datasets/master/fips-unemp-16.csv",
  header = TRUE,
  colClasses = c("fips" = "character")
)
head(df)
```

### Choropleth Map Using GeoJSON
```{r}
library(plotly.core)
library(jsonlite)

url <- "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/plotly/datasets/master/geojson-counties-fips.json"
counties <- fromJSON(url, simplifyVector = FALSE)
url2 <- "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/plotly/datasets/master/fips-unemp-16.csv"
df <- read.csv(url2, colClasses = c(fips = "character"))
g <- go_geo(
  scope = "usa",
  projection = go_geo_projection(type = "albers usa"),
  showlakes = TRUE,
  lakecolor = "white"
)

go_figure() |>
  add_choropleth(
    geojson = counties,
    locations = df$fips,
    z = df$unemp,
    colorscale = "Viridis",
    zmin = 0,
    zmax = 12,
    marker = go_choropleth_marker(line = go_choropleth_marker_line(width = 0)),
    colorbar = go_colorbar(title = "Unemployment Rate (%)")
  ) |>
  update_layout(title = "2016 US Unemployment by County", geo = g)
```
**Note** In this example we set `layout.geo.scope` to usa to automatically configure the map to display USA-centric data in an appropriate projection.

### Indexing by GeoJSON Properties

If the GeoJSON you are using either does not have an `id` field or you wish you use one of the keys in the `properties` field, you may use the `featureidkey` parameter to specify where to match the values of locations.

In the following GeoJSON object/data-file pairing, the values of `properties.district` match the values of the `district` column:
```{r}
library(plotly.core)
library(jsonlite)

url <- "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/plotly/datasets/master/election.geojson"
geojson <- fromJSON(url, simplifyVector = FALSE)
url2 <- "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/plotly/datasets/master/election.csv"
df <- read.csv(url2)

go_figure() |>
  add_choropleth(
    geojson = geojson,
    locations = df$district,
    z = df$Bergeron,
    colorscale = "Viridis",
    featureidkey = "properties.district",
    colorbar = go_colorbar(title = "Bergeron Votes")
  ) |>
  update_layout(
    geo = go_geo(fitbounds = "locations", visible = FALSE),
    title = "2013 Montreal Election"
  )
```
### Using Built-in Country and State Geometries
Plotly comes with two built-in geometries which do not require an external GeoJSON file:

1. USA States
2. Countries as defined in the Natural Earth dataset.

**Note and disclaimer:** cultural (as opposed to physical) features are by definition subject to change, debate and dispute. Plotly includes data from Natural Earth "as-is" and defers to the [Natural Earth policy regarding disputed borders](https://www.naturalearthdata.com/downloads/50m-cultural-vectors/50m-admin-0-countries-2/) which read:

> Natural Earth Vector draws boundaries of countries according to defacto status. We show who actually controls the situation on the ground.

To use the built-in countries geometry, provide `locations` as [three-letter ISO country codes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_3166-1_alpha-3).
```{r}
library(plotly.core)
df <- read.csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/plotly/datasets/master/2014_world_gdp_with_codes.csv")
df

df |>
  go_figure() |>
  add_choropleth(
    locations = ~CODE,
    z = ~GDP..BILLIONS.,
    text = ~COUNTRY,
    colorscale = "Blues"
  )
```

To use the USA States geometry, set `locationmode = "USA-states"` and provide `locations` as two-letter state abbreviations:
```{r}
library(plotly.core)
df <- read.csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/plotly/datasets/master/2011_us_ag_exports.csv")
df$hover <- with(df, paste(state, "<br>", "Beef", beef, "Dairy", dairy, "<br>",
                           "Fruits", total.fruits, "Veggies", total.veggies,
                           "<br>", "Wheat", wheat, "Corn", corn))

df |>
  go_figure() |>
  add_choropleth(
    locationmode = "USA-states",
    z = ~total.exports,
    text = ~hover,
    locations = ~code,
    colorscale = "Purples",
    colorbar = go_colorbar(title = "Millions USD")
  ) |>
  update_layout(
    title = "2011 US Agriculture Exports by State<br>(Hover for breakdown)"
  )
```

### Customize choropleth chart
```{r}
library(plotly.core)
df <- read.csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/plotly/datasets/master/2011_us_ag_exports.csv")
df$hover <- with(df, paste(state, "<br>", "Beef", beef, "Dairy", dairy, "<br>",
                           "Fruits", total.fruits, "Veggies", total.veggies,
                           "<br>", "Wheat", wheat, "Corn", corn))
# give state boundaries a white border
l <- go_choropleth_marker_line(color = "white", width = 2)
# specify some map projection/options
g <- go_geo(
  scope = "usa",
  projection = go_geo_projection(type = "albers usa"),
  showlakes = TRUE,
  lakecolor = "white"
)

df |>
  go_figure() |>
  add_choropleth(
    locationmode = "USA-states",
    z = ~total.exports,
    text = ~hover,
    locations = ~code,
    colorscale = "Purples",
    marker = go_choropleth_marker(line = l),
    colorbar = go_colorbar(title = "Millions USD")
  ) |>
  update_layout(
    title = "2011 US Agriculture Exports by State<br>(Hover for breakdown)",
    geo = g
  )
```

**Note** In this example we set `layout.geo.scope` to `usa` to automatically configure the map to display USA-centric data in an appropriate projection.

### World Choropleth Map

```{r}
library(plotly.core)

df <- read.csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/plotly/datasets/master/2014_world_gdp_with_codes.csv")

# light grey boundaries
l <- go_choropleth_marker_line(color = "grey", width = 0.5)

# specify map projection/options
g <- go_geo(
  showframe = FALSE,
  showcoastlines = FALSE,
  projection = go_geo_projection(type = "mercator")
)

df |>
  go_figure() |>
  add_choropleth(
    z = ~GDP..BILLIONS.,
    colorscale = "Blues",
    text = ~COUNTRY,
    locations = ~CODE,
    marker = go_choropleth_marker(line = l),
    colorbar = go_colorbar(title = "GDP Billions US$", tickprefix = "$")
  ) |>
  update_layout(
    title = '2014 Global GDP<br>Source:<a href="https://www.cia.gov/library/publications/the-world-factbook/fields/2195.html">CIA World Factbook</a>',
    geo = g
  )
```

### Choropleth Inset Map

```{r}
library(plotly.core)

df <- read.csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/plotly/datasets/master/2014_ebola.csv")
# restrict from June to September
df <- subset(df, Month %in% 6:9)
# ordered factor variable with month abbreviations
df$abbrev <- ordered(month.abb[df$Month], levels = month.abb[6:9])
# September totals
df9 <- subset(df, Month == 9)

# main map
g1 <- go_geo(
  scope = "africa",
  showframe = FALSE,
  showland = TRUE,
  landcolor = "rgb(229,229,229)",
  resolution = 50,
  showcoastlines = TRUE,
  countrycolor = "white",
  coastlinecolor = "white",
  projection = go_geo_projection(type = "mercator"),
  lonaxis = go_geo_lonaxis(range = c(-15, -5)),
  lataxis = go_geo_lataxis(range = c(0, 12)),
  domain = go_domain(x = c(0, 1), y = c(0, 1))
)

# inset map
g2 <- go_geo(
  scope = "africa",
  showframe = FALSE,
  showland = TRUE,
  landcolor = "rgb(229,229,229)",
  showcountries = FALSE,
  bgcolor = "rgba(255,255,255,0)",
  # the whole continent
  lonaxis = go_geo_lonaxis(range = c(-20, 55)),
  lataxis = go_geo_lataxis(range = c(-36, 38)),
  domain = go_domain(x = c(0, 0.6), y = c(0, 0.6))
)

# marker area proportional to the number of cases
sizeref <- 2 * max(df$Value) / 40^2

# one trace per month, coloured by the ordered factor (viridis)
fig <- df |>
  go_figure() |>
  add_scattergeo(
    lat = ~Lat,
    lon = ~Lon,
    text = ~paste(Value, "cases"),
    mode = "markers",
    marker = go_scattergeo_marker(
      color = ~abbrev,
      size = ~Value,
      sizemode = "area",
      sizeref = sizeref
    )
  )
# draw the largest (September) circles first, so the earlier months show on top
fig$data <- rev(fig$data)

fig |>
  add_scattergeo(
    lon = 21.0936,
    lat = 7.1881,
    text = "Africa",
    mode = "text",
    showlegend = FALSE,
    geo = "geo2"
  ) |>
  add_choropleth(
    data = df9,
    z = ~Month,
    locations = ~Country,
    locationmode = "country names",
    colorscale = list(c(0, "#F28E5C"), c(1, "#F28E5C")),
    marker = go_choropleth_marker(line = go_choropleth_marker_line(color = "black")),
    showscale = FALSE,
    geo = "geo2"
  ) |>
  update_layout(
    title = 'Ebola cases reported by month in West Africa 2014<br> Source: <a href="https://data.hdx.rwlabs.org/dataset/rowca-ebola-cases">HDX</a>',
    geo = g1,
    geo2 = g2
  )
```
